questions.prompt: A paddle learner practices balance on dry land but freezes when current touches the boat. What is the best next practice design?
choices: Move straight to open water so the real environment teaches quickly.
Repeat one recovery sequence in sheltered water, then test light current.
Stay on land until the sequence feels automatic without water present.
questions.explanation: Sheltered water keeps the condition present without full chaos. Open water is too broad, while dry land removes the variable that changes the skill.

questions.prompt: A drone pilot lands perfectly in a simulator but drifts in a light crosswind near trees. Which drill best fits condition-shaped practice?
choices: Buy a more advanced controller before returning to the field again.
Practice longer in the simulator until full confidence returns indoors.
Set two cones in an open field and drill crosswind landings.
questions.explanation: The cone lane isolates the crosswind landing in a safer live setting. Gear and simulator time avoid the condition causing the drift.

questions.prompt: On a low ski-patrol slope, a trainee wants to take a loaded sled on the full run, but the sled fishtails on the first loaded turn while the trainer is still walking beside him. What should happen?
choices: Repeat the loaded turn on a low slope with a trainer before advancing.
Practice unloaded turns until the sled feels less intimidating.
Try the full run once so the trainee understands the real stakes.
questions.explanation: The loaded turn is the live subskill. A low slope keeps progression bounded, while a full run adds risk and unloaded turns remove the key condition.

questions.prompt: During an outdoor portrait session, a photographer loses faces whenever clouds cross the sun, even though indoor exposure drills looked clean. Which variable should shape the next practice block?
choices: General composition, because it matters in every photo.
Camera brand settings, studied until the menu feels easy.
Changing light, tested through short exposure sets and histogram checks.
questions.explanation: Cloud cover is changing the task, so practice should answer that condition. Menus and composition may matter but do not target the live failure.

questions.prompt: An outdoor market vendor keeps practicing canopy setup in a garage, but the stall fails when wind hits the aisle. What is the better progression?
choices: Keep practicing in the garage until the steps are memorized perfectly.
Skip practice and ask neighboring vendors to hold the canopy during setup.
Isolate the windward-leg sequence with safe weights, then test it in light aisle gusts.
questions.explanation: The windward leg is where equipment and condition meet. Garage practice removes the wind, while improvising at the market avoids learning.

questions.prompt: A field technician levels a tripod well on pavement but fails on uneven soil. Which response uses the environment correctly?
choices: Return to pavement practice until the setup feels smooth and repeatable.
Level beside one trench and let the first real reading judge it.
Study tripod specifications before trying uneven soil again outside.
questions.explanation: Uneven soil is the condition that changes the setup. A real reading checks whether the staged practice still serves field accuracy.

questions.prompt: A learner says staged practice is fake because the real environment is harder, and wants to skip the cove, cones, and low slope for the full condition right away. What is the best correction?
choices: Staged practice is honest when it keeps the key environmental variable present at a safer scale.
Staged practice should avoid environmental pressure until confidence is complete.
The learner should enter full conditions immediately so fear disappears.
questions.explanation: A good staged subskill preserves the variable that matters while managing risk. Avoidance and full chaos both fail the design standard.

questions.prompt: A wind-shaped skill keeps failing at the exact moment the gust arrives, and the learner starts researching equipment specs late at night instead of touching the live condition. What question should come first?
choices: Which product has the best expert reviews for advanced learners?
Which condition is changing the task, and what small live subskill can meet it safely?
How long should a full outdoor session last to build courage?
questions.explanation: The task starts with the condition and a trainable live slice. Specs or courage sessions can distract from the variable that actually breaks the skill.

questions.prompt: Two learners practice condition-shaped skills. One stays in sheltered drills forever. The other tests one subskill under a low-risk real condition. Which is stronger?
choices: The low-risk live test, because the condition must judge transfer.
The sheltered learner, because clean indoor reps matter more than transfer.
The equipment researcher, because better gear removes most conditions.
questions.explanation: Shelter helps only when it keeps a path back to the real condition. A low-risk live test lets wind, current, slope, or ground reveal whether the subskill transfers.

reviewCards.front: A kayak drill works in a cove but fails once current enters the stroke. What makes the skill condition-shaped?
reviewCards.back: The environment changes the assignment. Wind, current, slope, light, ground, or equipment behavior becomes part of what must be practiced.

reviewCards.front: When is staged isolation honest in an outdoor or field skill?
reviewCards.back: It is honest when the key condition stays present at a safer, smaller scale and the result gets tested by the real environment.

reviewCards.front: A learner gets smooth indoors but fails when wind, slope, or glare returns. Which risk is showing up?
reviewCards.back: The learner may get smooth at a version of the skill that never meets the variable that makes the real task difficult.

reviewCards.front: How do you choose the first live subskill?
reviewCards.back: Name the environmental variable that breaks the skill, then choose the smallest repeatable action that can meet that variable safely.

reviewCards.front: What should equipment details never replace?
reviewCards.back: They should never replace contact with the trainable condition. Gear knowledge helps only when it supports the live subskill being tested.

implementationPlan.coreSkill: Design a live but bounded practice slice. Identify the condition that changes the task, isolate one subskill, and test it under a low-risk version of that condition.

ifThenPlans.plan: If a skill changes with weather or terrain, then practice one subskill where that condition is present but bounded.
If clean setup fails outside, then repeat the setup on the real surface and judge it by one field reading.
If light, noise, or crowd movement changes the result, then build a short drill around that variable instead of practicing every setting.
If full conditions carry risk, then lower the scale while preserving the variable that makes the skill real.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Name one condition-shaped skill and define the smallest live subskill that could face a real but low-risk version of the environment.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Once this week, audit one sheltered drill and ask whether it is preparing real contact or helping you avoid the condition that matters.
